function.name: calculate_electric_current
function.description: Calculate the electric current through a conductor given voltage and resistance. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

voltage.description: The voltage across the conductor in Volts. This is a float type value.

resistance.description: The resistance of the conductor in Ohms. This is a float type value.

conductance.description: The conductance of the conductor in Siemens. Optional if resistance is provided. Default: 0.3 This is a float type value.

message.content:
Electricity isn’t the discovery of a single person—it’s a natural phenomenon that has been known since ancient times. Here’s a quick overview of the key figures who helped uncover its nature:

| Era | Scientist | Contribution |
|-----|-----------|--------------|
| **Ancient Greece** | **Thales of Miletus** (c. 600 BCE) | Noted that rubbing amber produced static electricity. |
| **16th–17th Century** | **William Gilbert** (1544–1603) | Published *De Magnete* (1600), distinguishing magnetism from static electricity and coined the term “electricity.” |
| **18th Century** | **Benjamin Franklin** (1706–1790) | Conducted the famous kite experiment, showing that lightning is electrical. Introduced the concepts of positive/negative charge and the conservation of charge. |
| **Late 18th Century** | **Alessandro Volta** (1745–1827) | Invented the voltaic pile (the first battery) in 1800, providing a steady source of electric current. |
| **Early 19th Century** | **Michael Faraday** (1791–1867) | Discovered electromagnetic induction (Faraday’s law) and developed the first electric motor. |
| **19th Century** | **James Clerk Maxwell** (1831–1879) | Unified electricity and magnetism into Maxwell’s equations, predicting electromagnetic waves. |
| **Late 19th Century** | **Thomas Edison** (1847–1931) | Developed practical incandescent lighting and the electrical distribution system. |
| **Late 19th Century** | **Nikola Tesla** (1856–1943) | Pioneered alternating current (AC) power systems and wireless transmission. |

So, while no single person “discovered” electricity, the cumulative work of these and many other scientists turned a mysterious natural phenomenon into the foundation of modern electrical science and technology.
